name: SC-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deep-red district: partisan lean of about 21 points Republican
Freshman incumbent Biggs holds a roughly 5-to-1 fundraising advantage
Prediction markets price the Democratic upset at only about 3%
No public polling and minimal Democratic fundraising in the race
model.rationale: The R+21 district, Biggs's large money edge, and market pricing near 3% for Democrats all point the same direction, and even a nationally favorable climate for Democrats only narrows the expected gap modestly. With no polling or expert ratings suggesting competition, there is no evidence warranting a move away from a double-digit Republican margin.
model.watch: A major scandal involving Biggs or an unusually strong Democratic wave in the national environment would be the most plausible path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 3rd District is among the most Republican seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 21 points toward the GOP. Sheri Biggs, a freshman who won the seat in 2024, is seeking a second term with a decisive financial edge: she has raised about $505,000 and holds roughly $219,000 on hand, while Democrat Eunice Lehmacher has raised about $93,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls have surveyed the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 3% chance of an upset. Even accounting for a more favorable national climate for Democratic candidates this cycle, the district's fundamentals make the incumbent a heavy favorite. Biggs is expected to win re-election comfortably by a double-digit margin, with any meaningful Democratic upside limited to a strong national wave.
